Yes, if nobody outside your own machines has ever run a build with `is.waiwai.dictation`. If anyone has, I'd keep it. The rule is there because of what a rename costs existing installs, not because the string can't change. As the owner, you can lift it, but the rules file and the docs would need updating so nobody "fixes" it back.

**If a build with the old ID has shipped to real users:**
- macOS ties Accessibility permission to the bundle ID, so every user would have to re-grant it. For a dictation app, that looks like a broken app.
- The renamed app is a different app to the system. It gets a separate preferences domain, Application Support folder, Keychain items, and login-item registration, so you'd need migration code.
- Sparkle may refuse to update across a bundle ID change, and I'm not certain how your Sparkle version handles it. Existing users could be stranded on the old app unless you test an old-to-new update first.

**If it has never shipped (only dev or internal builds):**
- The rename is cheap, and launch is the last good time to do it.
- Your own machines will need to re-grant Accessibility once.
- The Sparkle EdDSA key is unaffected, so keep it. The signing rules are also unaffected, so keep signing nested code inside-out and don't use `codesign --deep`.
- Change the ID everywhere it appears: Info.plist, the Xcode project, entitlements, the provisioning or notarization setup, the appcast and release scripts, URL schemes, and `docs/release.md` and `AGENTS.md`.

Has any build with `is.waiwai.dictation` gone to testers or users outside your own machines? If it has, I'd keep the ID. The brand can change in the app name and UI without touching the identifier.

I have no files in this session, so I can't check any of this against the repo. When you're ready to do it, I can list every place the ID appears.
